newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Women suffer "hall of shame" in South Asia - report.
newsitem.headline: Women suffer "hall of shame" in South Asia - report.

text.p: Women suffer worse discrimination in South Asia than in most other parts of the world, said a human development report on Wednesday that cited the region as a "hall of shame".

"To be a woman in South Asia is to be a non-person," said the report by Pakistan's Human Development Centre (HDC), which said its study was assisted by field offices of the United Nations Development Programme.
"From cradle to grave, there is a record of preferential treatment for boys...and a litany of violence against women: from infanticide to child abuse to rapes to dowry deaths to pyre-burning."
South Asia was the only region where men outnumbered women in the total population, the report said.
The global ratio of females to males was 106 to 100. In South Asia, it was only 94 to 100, it said.
"Compared to the global norms, about 74 million women are simply missing in South Asia, the unfortunate victims of social and economic neglect," it said.
It said that in Pakistan, 12 percent more girls than boys died in the one-to-four age group.
"The missing women of South Asia are a telling neglect of the basic rights of women in this region," it said.
"South Asia stands alone in this hall of shame. In no other region do men outnumber women."
The report said neglect of women in South Asia was directly linked to economic status.
"It is a pervasive phenomenon," it said, adding: "Punjab is the richest state in India but it has the lowest ratio of women to men (only 86 to 100)."

HDC president, Mahbub-ul-Haq, a former Pakistani finance minister, said South Asia had the lowest ratio of female administrators and managers to men -- only three percent compared to 20 percent in Latin America.

"And such indices of gender disparity persist in a region where four out of seven countries (Bangladesh, India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka) can boast of a female head of government at present or in the recent past," Haq said.
The other three countries of the region are Bhutan, Nepal and the Maldives.
